headline: Southborough officials advanced plans for a Route 9 wastewater system and District Improvement Financing while filling appointments for the Neary School project.
synopsis: In April 2026, Southborough boards focused on major infrastructure planning, municipal policies, and development reviews. The Select Board and Wastewater Study Committee progressed on an estimated $40 million to $50 million Route 9 wastewater concept, aiming for District Improvement Financing authorization at the fall Special Town Meeting. The School Committee appointed two members to the Elementary School Building Committee for the Neary School project. The Planning Board addressed scenic road trees, required six replacement trees for an unauthorized removal on Route 9, and moved forward with native planting regulations. Meanwhile, the Conservation Commission adopted updated conservation land use regulations and continued hearings on a proposed two-building apartment project at 0 Southville Road.

top_items.title: Route 9 wastewater planning and committee charge extension
top_items.why: Officials reviewed an estimated $40 million to $50 million wastewater concept and extended the planning committee's charge through June 2027.
top_items.body: The Regional Wastewater Planning Committee and Wastewater Study Committee presented updates on establishing a sewer collection and treatment system along the Route 9 commercial corridor. Technical needs include a 15- to 20-acre leaching area, prompting committee members to explore connecting non-contiguous parcels using pump systems. The committee aims to bring a District Improvement Financing (DIF) proposal and design funds to the fall Special Town Meeting, and the Select Board voted 4-0-1 to extend the committee's charge through June 30, 2027.

top_items.title: Elementary School Building Committee appointments for Neary project
top_items.why: The School Committee voted 3-0 to appoint Craig Williams and Heather McCloud to the building committee.
top_items.body: The School Committee selected two appointees for the newly formed Elementary School Building Committee guiding the Neary School building project. Members prioritized candidates with current educational experience, selecting Craig Williams for his administrative background in school transitions and Heather McCloud for her focus on classroom functionality and special education.

top_items.title: Hearing continued on 0 Southville Road apartment buildings
top_items.why: The Conservation Commission continued review of a Notice of Intent for two proposed apartment buildings to May 14, 2026.
top_items.body: Apartments at Southville Road LLC presented Notice of Intent and Stormwater Management Permit applications to construct two apartment buildings and supporting infrastructure. Discussions centered on roughly 4,500 square feet of disturbance within the outer riparian riverfront area, peer review by Lucas Environmental, and how local wetland bylaws align with MBTA Communities Act zoning. The commission voted 5-0 to continue the hearing.

top_items.title: Developer ordered to replace unauthorized tree removal on Route 9
top_items.why: Capital Group Properties must donate six replacement trees after removing a public shade tree at 154 Turnpike Road without town approval.
top_items.body: Following a joint public hearing with the tree warden, the Planning Board determined that Capital Group Properties failed to follow proper procedures when removing a decaying public shade tree at Turnpike Road and Breakneck Hill Road. The board approved remediation requiring the developer to provide six three-inch caliper replacement trees for the town to plant. In a separate vote, the board continued the site plan modification hearing for 154 Turnpike Road to May 11, 2026.

top_items.title: Select Board approves senior tax work-off and grants policies
top_items.why: The Select Board unanimously adopted a 40-slot Senior Tax Work-Off Policy and established a municipal Grants Management Policy.
top_items.body: The Select Board updated eligibility rules for the Senior Tax Work-Off Policy and voted unanimously to set the number of available positions at 40. The board also approved a new Grants Management Policy designed to establish municipal oversight and ensure grant applications do not generate unexpected personnel costs or unfunded operating expenses for the town.

top_items.title: Planning Board prepares native plant site regulations
top_items.why: The board agreed to draft native plant standards as formal site plan regulations for consideration in May.
top_items.body: Open Space Preservation Commission Chair Freddie Gillespie presented a draft policy promoting native plants, soft landings, and invasive species management for projects subject to Planning Board review. Board members supported incorporating native planting standards into site plan regulations, while deciding that more complex invasive species management requirements should be drafted separately.

top_items.title: Conservation Commission adopts town land use regulations
top_items.why: The commission voted 5-0 to adopt formal regulations governing public use of town conservation parcels.
top_items.body: The Conservation Commission voted unanimously to formally adopt land use regulations under Section 43-2 of the Southborough Town Code. The rules incorporate feedback from the Breakneck Hill Stewardship Committee to govern public use of municipal conservation areas, with future amendments expected to examine exterior light trespass from abutting properties.
